title: Why Guests Call to Check a Booking That Already Exists
summary: A call to check an existing booking means a confirmation failed: the email, the hotel's view of the booking, or a promised callback. How to find which one.
body_markdown:
Common questions


## FAQ


### Why do hotel guests call to confirm a booking they already made?


Usually because a confirmation signal failed. The confirmation email did not arrive, the hotel could not yet see a booking made on a booking site, or a promised confirmation callback never came.


In one published sample of 8,944 calls to eleven German hotels over 30 days, booking confirmation was 10.8% of every call, and guests often called because a confirmation email did not arrive or because they wanted to hear that the reservation was really in the system. That sample is not a market average.


### Why can a hotel not find a reservation made on a booking site?


A reservation made on a booking site passes through at least one other system before it reaches the hotel's property management system, or someone has to enter it by hand. The guest receives the booking site's confirmation right away.


Until the reservation arrives at the hotel, reception cannot find it by reference number, and a guest who calls in that gap is asking about a booking the desk cannot see.


### What should a hotel do when a guest says the confirmation email never arrived?


Check the address on the booking first, because one wrong letter sends the confirmation to nobody. Then resend it and ask the guest to check spam and promotions folders. If the same complaint keeps coming back, the fault is upstream, in how addresses are captured at booking or how the confirmation is sent.


A one-week tally of these calls at the desk shows whether it is a pattern or a one-off.


### Why are guests calling hotels to check messages about their booking?


Because fake booking messages have become convincing. Which? has documented messages inside Booking.com's own app asking guests to pay to "secure your booking", and Booking.com says it would never ask customers for payment information by email, chat, text or phone.


In June 2024, Booking.com's internet safety chief told the BBC there had been "anywhere from a 500 to a 900% increase" in travel scams over the previous 18 months. A guest who doubts a message checks with the hotel.


### Do AI agents call hotels?


Yes. Front desks take confirmation calls from software acting for a guest or a booking site. Google places automated calls to businesses on customers' behalf, to book appointments and confirm product and service details, across most of the United States and in select other regions.


Booking sites also run AI agents that call hotel front desks to look up a booking confirmation or a reference number. The question is the one a guest would ask.


### How many hotels confirm bookings by calling the guest back?


At least 13.3% of 26,707 hotels with a live website in Germany, Austria and Switzerland confirm bookings by manual callback. The figure is a floor, because it only counts hotels that say so on their own website. For those hotels, a confirmation is a promised phone call.


When the callback does not come, the call the hotel meant to make arrives instead as an inbound call from the guest.
